title: Extension process protocol
description: The process protocol (version 1) between the hub and an extension's program: one JSON object a line on stdin / stdout (or a unix socket), keys in snake_case. Also what the apps send the hub to draw a slot.

Frame.description: One line: a request {id, method, params}, an answer {id, result} or {id, error}, or an event {event, params}.

message.description: For people; never a secret or a message's body.

code.description: One of ErrorCode, or an extension point's own (not_found, invalid, conflict…).

Method.description: Methods of the base; every other method is <namespace>.<method>, the namespace an extension point's.

AuthStatus.description: auth.status and auth.logout: the extension's sign-in now (manifest.auth).

message.description: For people: why it is in error, what is signed in.

AuthStepParams.description: auth.step: step "" starts over; values are the fields of the step before.

AuthPrompt.description: auth.step's answer, the connectors' Prompt: fields to fill, a device code (url to open, user_code to enter) or a QR code (url, scanned with another app), or done. For device_code and qr the app asks the same step again (no values) every interval seconds.

kind.description: Empty: fields to fill; device_code; qr.

InitializeParams.description: What the hub sends first. The extension is under extension; hubs before the rename (#1844) send it as plugin, newer hubs send both.

config.description: The configuration with the schema's defaults filled in.

active.description: The contributions this run is for, by extension point.

contributions_to_me.description: The contributions of the other extensions that are on to the points it exports, by its point id (event extension.contributions_changed says them again when they change).

item.description: The contribution, as that extension's manifest wrote it.

locale.description: The user's language (zh-Hans, en, ja; see docs/protocol/i18n.md); empty means zh-Hans.

url.description: The hub's API on this machine, for the token below.

token.description: A token of the scopes it was granted (permissions.hub): new each start.

ui_page_cancellation.description: Request-ID scoped rpc.cancel for mounted page lifecycle calls only.

UIParams.description: ui.render's and ui.action's parameters: what to draw, where, for whom.

UIImageParams.description: ui.image's parameters (UI version 6): the hub asks the extension for a picture it drew as a ref, for the ui contribution that drew it. width is the pixel width the app wants (320, 640, 1280 or 2048; 0 when it says nothing); the extension may ignore it.

UIImage.description: What ui.image answers: the picture's bytes in base64 (png, jpeg, webp or gif, at most 4 MB decoded and 8192 pixels a side; the hub reads the type from the bytes, not from mime) and how long the hub may keep it (seconds, 60 when absent; a camera 5 to 10, a still 86400).

meta.description: The connector's own record of what the item gathers, as stored; null when it has none.

BadgeEvent.description: ui.badge, sent by an extension: the badge on its nav_page's entry (no text clears it).

InvalidateEvent.description: ui.invalidate, sent by an extension (UI version 3): what it draws changed; the apps on screen draw it again (contribution: one ui; empty: all of the extension's).

UIContext.description: What an app says when it draws a slot: for whom and where (the hub checks it and hands the extension UIParams).

stream.description: Explicit stream opt-in, independent of ui_version. Absent means snapshot-only. Contract only: no current client or hub advertises it.

UIRequest.description: An app's POST …/-/ui/{ui}: without action it draws, with one a control was used.

UIPlace.description: Where an extension draws something, as the hub lists it (GET …/-/ui). The new API names the extension extension / extension_name; the old one plugin / plugin_name.

WidgetPlace.description: A widget an extension draws outside the app (GET …/extensions/-/widgets; docs "System placements").

WidgetRequest.description: An app's POST …/extensions/{id}/-/widget/{ui}: context.size is the family it draws (WidgetFamily).

WidgetAnswer.description: A widget's view, held to what the family draws, and until when the hub keeps it (the app's timeline's next entry).

DeviceWidget.description: A widget a device has on a screen (PUT /api/v1/devices/{id}/widgets): the hub wakes that device when it changes.

WidgetPush.description: extension_widget in a background push (content-available): a widget the device has changed; the app reloads its timelines.

ShortcutPlace.description: An extension's action the system runs (GET …/extensions/-/shortcuts).

ShortcutRequest.description: An app's POST …/extensions/{id}/-/shortcut/{sid}: the params' values (strings) and the context (tz, locale, platform, ui_version).

ShortcutRunParams.description: shortcut.run's parameters: which shortcut, its values, for whom.

ShortcutResult.description: What shortcut.run answers (and the app gets): a sentence Siri says or shows, and a view held to the large widget's subset (the result card).

NotifyAction.description: A button on an extension's notification (POST /api/v1/notify actions, at most 3). A tap runs ui.action on the notification's ui with this id; input asks for a line of text first (values.text).

foreground.description: Open the app to run it; otherwise it runs in the background and its toast is shown as a notification.

ErrorSource.description: Which part of Persona an error report comes from.

ErrorKind.description: What an error report is: a caught exception, a crash (the app died), an ANR (it hung), a Go panic, an error line of a log.

ErrorFrame.description: One frame of a stack trace.

in_app.description: Persona's own code, not a library's or the system's.

ErrorException.description: One exception of a report; frames innermost last (the order Sentry uses).

ErrorBreadcrumb.description: Something that happened before the error: a screen opened, a request failed. Code-chosen short text, no user content.

ErrorReport.description: An error or crash of the hub or a device (docs/extensions/extensions.md "Error reports"). Clients send it to POST /api/v1/error-reports; the manager scrubs it and adds fingerprint, count and received_at before an extension gets it.

id.description: Made by the sender; the same id again (a retry) is dropped.

device_model.description: The model only, never an id of the device.

previous_launch.description: It happened in an earlier run of the app and is sent now.

fingerprint.description: Set by the manager: reports with the same one are the same problem.

count.description: Set by the manager: how many of this fingerprint it folded into this one (1 or more).

ErrorReportsDeliver.description: error_reports.deliver, sent to an extension with an error_reports contribution: reports, already scrubbed, deduplicated and rate limited. A notification: no answer, not sent again.

AuthRelayCompleteParams.description: auth_relay.complete's parameters: an authorization link one of the user's Agents stopped at, on a host and path the contribution names. The manager has checked that the Agent's own command printed it on one of the user's computers. The link is a secret while it lives: never log it.

AuthRelayStatus.description: How auth_relay.complete ended: done (authorized, the Agent can go on), manual (not one it completes: the user's), failed (one it completes, but it did not go through).

AuthRelayReason.description: Why it was not done: not_handled (not a link it completes), not_signed_in (its account is not signed in for the page), new_permissions (the page asks for more than was granted before), app_not_allowed (the extension's own settings leave this app to the user), unknown_page (not the page it knows), unavailable (what it completes them with can't be reached), not_confirmed (it clicked, the page never said it was done), expired (the link is no longer valid).

AuthRelayResult.description: What auth_relay.complete answers. Never the link, a token or a page's text.

app.description: The app the page authorized (or asked to), as the page names it.

SecretPurpose.description: What a secret value is resolved for: kind extension (an extension's secret, id its id), launcher (a launcher's or model provider's key, id its name, machine the computer it goes to) or agent_run (handed to one Agent run after the user approved it on the phone, id the variable's name, machine and session the Agent's).

SecretsDescribeParams.description: secrets.describe's parameters: a reference of one of the contribution's schemes.

SecretsDescribeResult.description: What secrets.describe answers: words for people (the item and field), never a value.

SecretsResolveParams.description: secrets.resolve's parameters: the reference and what it is resolved for. Only the manager calls it.

SecretsResolveResult.description: What secrets.resolve answers: the value, at most 16 KB. Errors: not_found, not_signed_in, rate_limited (data.retry_after), refused.

SecretsUsedEvent.description: secrets.used (an event to the provider, no answer): a reference it resolved was used, for the usage record its own page shows. Never the value.

approved_by.description: settings (a reference saved in Settings), rule (an Always rule) or the approving device's id.

ExtensionNotification.description: extension_notification in an extension's alert push: whose it is, the page a tap opens (ui with state) and its buttons (category ext.<extension>.<hash of the action ids>, registered by the app as it meets it).
